restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each pads to m || 0x86 in a single 136-byte rate block under the SHA3 0x06 suffix and pad10*1.
Uses the complete fixed-zero-state SHA3-256 sponge with prefix Keccak-f[1600] rounds 0 through 4 on every permutation call.

Algorithm: R = 2^13 randomized two-round connector executions for the published trail core No. 3 of Guo et al. (ePrint 2019/147) with fixed-bit parameter p = 8, each producing an affine message space; every message m is hashed as H(m) and H(m XOR delta); first verified distinct-message pair is returned.
All connector work, retries, randomness, hashing, scanning and final verification are charged; there is no restart beyond the fixed R schedule.

Analytical construction adapting published results; no full-scale execution, no submitted executable, no certificate; the published 1084-bit witness is cited as permutation-level evidence only and is not in the byte-string domain.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement; the conservative scalar bound is 60 under collision-frontier-v5 with declared heuristics h1-h4.

heuristics.statement: A two-round connector for GLL+19 trail core No. 3 with byte-aligned padding (p = 8 fixed tail bits instead of the published p = 4) returns an affine message space of dimension DF >= 25 on the exact profile.
heuristics.scope: Prefix rounds 0-1 of Keccak-f[1600], rate 1088 / capacity 512, 135-byte messages; the DF floor enters the success accounting in proof Section 4.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured DF = 37 at p = 4 (paper Table 6). Byte alignment adds four linear constraints on message bits, entering the paper's degree-of-freedom bookkeeping additively (their formula (11) and TDF threshold), giving an expected DF near 33; the floor 25 is eight bits below that expectation. The authors note their TDF threshold is pessimistic.
heuristics.limitations: The paper does not analyze byte-aligned inputs; if DF falls below ~24 the success floor is not met (the algorithm remains correctly charged and simply fails).

heuristics.statement: Each tested pair (m, m XOR delta) follows trail core No. 3 over prefix rounds 2-4 to a zero difference on the 256 digest bits with probability at least 2^-36.70.
heuristics.scope: Prefix rounds 2,3,4 of the exact profile; per-pair event over the connector-produced pair distribution.
heuristics.extrapolation: The trail acts on state differences, which do not depend on message-bit encoding, so byte alignment does not perturb it. The reported 2^-36.70 figure already aggregates multiple trails of the last two rounds. The published Table 17 pair was verified to traverse this exact permutation under verifier/keccak.py rounds 0-4, confirming round convention and encoding.
heuristics.limitations: It is a reported differential probability, not a proof of the induced pair distribution; conditional dependence between the connector output distribution and the trail is assumed benign, as in the paper's own accounting.

heuristics.statement: Pair-collision events across the R = 2^13 randomized connector executions and within each affine space count as independent Bernoulli trials for the purpose of summing expected colliding pairs.
heuristics.scope: Randomized connector retry protocol of the paper applied 2^13 times with fresh coins; Poisson/Poisson-trial counting of Section 4.
heuristics.extrapolation: The same sufficiency convention (DF > w) underlies the published attack; each rerun samples a fresh randomized beta1/linear-system instance.
heuristics.limitations: Systematic correlation between subspaces would shrink the effective pair count; the declared floor absorbs up to ~2^6 adverse correlation before the 0.39 gate fails.

heuristics.statement: Each connector execution costs at most 2^46 charged units, i.e. the published 428.8 CPU core-hours convert to at most ~2^56.4 ordinary 256-bit word-ops (a ~2^35.8 ops/s/core envelope) plus all retry and bookkeeping overhead.
heuristics.scope: The connector stage only; brute force is charged separately at 2^49 units.
heuristics.extrapolation: Published single-core timing converted with a deliberately inflated instruction rate; the claimed total 2^60 has ~2 bits of headroom over the summed terms.
heuristics.limitations: It is a stated envelope rather than an instruction trace; a reconstruction several times looser still leaves the total below 2^62.
